title: One-off triple-merge debug notes
content:
Context
---
Working quick notes on a weird failure mode in the latest adjudication sample: cases where three overlapping candidate spans keep getting merged incorrectly by the cleanup pipeline. This is a personal scratchpad — half hypothesis, half small-run instructions. Goal: produce a tiny, deterministic rule set we can ship into cleanup v0.33 to reduce churn and labeler confusion.

Observed problem pattern
1) Three candidate spans overlapping in a chain (A overlaps B, B overlaps C) where A and C do not fully contain each other.
2) Automatic merge heuristic currently prefers longest-span-first then proximity; that ends up merging A+B and B+C sequentially and producing an overly permissive union (A..C) that sweeps unrelated punctuation or trailing text.
3) Edge triggers: possessives ("Acme's product X"), intra-span commas, and trailing prepositions ("for Acme product X") where the union pulls the preposition.

Why it matters
- Downstream model training treats unions as ground truth for positive spans — extra words add noise and hurt precision.
- Labeler adjudication keeps reverting merges and creates churn loops in the queue.

Initial manual triage examples (raw -> mistaken merged span -> desired outcome)
- "Acme's new Widget 2, v2.1" -> merged becomes "Acme's new Widget 2, v2.1" (okay) but observed where union added leading "for " producing "for Acme's new Widget 2, v2.1" -> desired: keep span starting at "Acme's" not including preceding preposition.
- "Acme Widget" + "Widget 2" + "Widget 2 v2.1" -> union produced "Acme Widget 2 v2.1" (removes comma boundaries) -> desired: prefer inner-most product span ("Widget 2 v2.1") and attach company only if explicit contiguous token (no punctuation between).
- "service: alpha / beta" splits into 3 spans; union swallowed the slash and produced a single long token that breaks tokenizers -> desired: keep as separate service names.

Proposed lightweight rules (ordered)
1) Longest-not-always: prefer "max-token-score" where score = tokens_in_span - boundary_penalty. boundary_penalty = 1 if span starts/ends with common preposition or punctuation (for, with, :, /, ,). This protects against absorbing leading prepositions.
2) Contiguity check: only merge spans across punctuation if punctuation is explicitly alphanumeric connector (dash, dot) and not a separator (comma, slash, colon, parentheses).
3) Ownership/possessive anchor: if a span begins with a possessive (like "Acme's"), prefer spans that start at that possessive rather than expanding backwards.
4) Nested-product preference: when spans appear to be product/variant chains (regex heuristics: contains digits, v\d+, v\d+\.\d+ or version-like tokens), prefer the most specific span (longest in character length among version-like candidates) and drop company if separated by punctuation.
5) Three-chain breaker: when merging would result in a span that is > 1.5x longer than the median candidate in the chain, insert adjudication flag instead of auto-merge. This means small ambiguous cases still auto-merge, but not big sweeps.

Quick labeler guidance (for release note)
- If you see three overlapping spans and the union pulls in helpers like "for", "on", or leading dates, mark "needs-adjudication" instead of fixing manually unless very obvious.
- Prefer keeping the innermost most product/identifier span when unsure.
- If possessive present, anchor to the possessive token as the start.

Sampling plan for validating rules
- Pull 200 random chain-of-3 events from recent adjudication logs (last 30 days).
- Manually label gold for 50 (fast triage) and run rules on all 200; compute precision delta relative to current pipeline.
- Pay particular attention to punctuation tokens [",", ":", "/"] — strata sample so at least 80 examples include one of them.

Quick test scripts (notes to self)
- small extractor: tools/samples/chain_extractor.py --min-chain 3 --since 2025-01-01 --out small-chain-sample.json
- local merge sim: ./scripts/merge_sim.sh small-chain-sample.json --rules candidate-scoring-v0.1
- sample adjudication job: run on staging adjudicator with sample flag to force human check for >1.5x rule.

Open questions / stuff to decide
- Are we comfortable hard-coding the 1.5x threshold? Might prefer percentile-based (90th pct) computed per-batch. Tradeoff: complexity vs immediate wins.\- How many labeler flips are acceptable per week? If this change reduces flips but increases adjudication hits, net workload might not improve. Need metric: flips per 1000 spans and adjudications per 1000 spans.
- Is there a taxonomy for "product-like" spans we can reuse (we have product_names table but messy)? Might be worth a quick fuzzy-match pass rather than regex-only.

Action Items
- [ ] Extract 200 chain-3 sample (me, 2025-02-13)
- [ ] Build quick scoring function and run local sim (Diego, 2025-02-17)
- [ ] Draft short labeler note for QA (Priya, 2025-02-18)
- [ ] Decide threshold style (percentile vs multiplier) after initial sim (team, 2025-02-21)

Mini-adjudication checklist (for labelers when they see these in queue)
1) Read raw sentence; locate nearest punctuation markers around chain.
2) Ask: Does union include a standalone preposition or date? If yes -> split.
3) If tokens include version pattern (v1, v2.0), prefer the version-containing span.
4) If possessive present, anchor to possessive start.
5) If ambiguous after steps above, mark needs-adjudication.

Notes to future me
- Keep heuristics simple and easily tunable flags. Don’t bake complicated ML matching into the cleanup stage — move heavy fuzzy-match later if needed.
- This doc: ephemeral. If rules show >5% improvement in precision on sample, lift into cleanup config and write short changelog entry.

Snowball thought: maybe a tiny ML discriminator that looks at candidate-union char-length ratio + punctuation features could predict "bad-union" with high precision and low recall (which is fine). Could try a tiny logistic reg with 3 features: union_len / median_len, contains_preposition_flag, num_punct_sep. Quick prototype after initial sim.

End.
